docs.actionable.component: `Actionable` is the atom a CONTROL carries: it names the intent a press emits. A button, a menu
item, a toggle's tap target — all of them are ordinary elements that happen to carry this.
The intent is a NAME, never a callback. A node travels: into a snapshot, over a wire, into a
second screen's projection — and a function survives none of those trips. So the field is a
registry ref, and what the verb DOES is the registry's business or the consumer's.
```ts
import { node, Bounded, Actionable, activate } from "game-kit"
const item = node("flipItem",
Bounded({ bounds: rect(2, 0.6) }),
Actionable({ action: "flip" }))
activate(item)                    // "flip" — the ref to emit
activate(node("plate"))           // undefined — nothing fires
## There is no `disabled`
A control that cannot be pressed is one that does not carry the capability. No atom, an unmet
requirement, or a ref that names nothing all come back as `undefined`, so a caller never has to
ask which kind of no it got. Greyness is a CONSEQUENCE a game draws from the refusal — never a
field that could disagree with it.
## Which verb, and about what
`Actionable` says WHICH verb; `Valued` carries what rides with it. The `button()` preset takes
both as `action` and `means`, and a control may honestly carry either alone: a menu item is all
verb, a drop target is all payload.
## Where a menu's items come from
Not from here. `actionsOf(node)` derives them from the capabilities the node already carries —
a `Flippable` can be flipped, a `Tiltable` can be tapped — so a card never advertises a flip it
cannot perform. This atom is the other half: the item that carries one of those names.
docs.actionable.menu: This IS a context menu, and every item in it was DERIVED. Nothing here writes out "Flip" and
"Tap": `actionsOf(card)` reads the capabilities the card already carries and returns the verbs
they imply. Turn a capability off with the knobs and its item leaves the menu by itself — a card
cannot advertise a flip it cannot perform, because nobody ever typed the offer.
Press an item and the card answers. Each item is a `button()` carrying `Actionable`, and the
handler is the whole of a press handler: ask `activate(control)` what it emits, stop if it emits
nothing. No `disabled` was consulted, because there is none to consult.
Watch which verbs the KIT performs. `flip` and `roll` ship a `perform` in their registry record,
so the kit returns the changed node itself. `tap` does not — it is a pure query, and walking the
tilt stops is this page's own answer to it. The control cannot tell the difference and must not:
it emits a name and stops there.
The menu carries `orientation: "viewer"`, which terminates the chain of angles. That is why a
context menu on a turned seat needs no camera of its own — the words stay upright by the same
